Thanks again for a productive demo last week. Legal at ArborHealth pushed back on a few clauses in the MSA and order form related to: output ownership, training data use, and a general feedback license. They attached an annotated MSA with in-line comments. High level asks from their counsel:

- They want explicit confirmation that ArborHealth retains exclusive ownership of any customer data + any customer-provided prompts/descriptions.
- They request a carveout so Redwood cannot use ArborHealth customer outputs to retrain models (no training on customer-derived outputs or prompts).
- A time-boxed telemetry/extract approach for safety/bug fixes (they are open to limited, aggregated telemetry for debugging but want opt-out controls).

Can your legal/procurement team review and propose language we can present back? We're trying to keep the order form moving — I think Arbor's procurement wants a firm path to sign this month if we can address ownership/training in the order form rather than an enterprise amendment.

Soren — thanks for sending and for the clear summary. Looping in Monica (Customer Ops) and Ben (Contracts) so we can give a concise proposal.

Quick priorities from our side before legal dives in:
1) We agree on customer data ownership — Redwood will not claim title to customer-provided data, prompts, or records. We typically include language that assigns customer content back to the customer and confirms Redwood's service is provided under a license.
2) Training carveout — we can offer a strict opt-in for any training on customer data or customer outputs. For Hosted customers on standard order forms we require explicit opt-in (checkbox/contracted scope). For Dedicated/Private deployments, training is never performed without a separate agreement.
3) Telemetry/bug-fix telemetry — propose aggregated, non-identifying telemetry for safety and performance; allow an opt-out at the tenant level with a narrow exception for security incidents.

Ben/Monica: can you confirm recommended clause text and whether we need an order-form exhibit (e.g., Exhibit B: Data & Training) vs inline order form language? Soren — if you can highlight the most sensitive language in the doc (the specific bracketed lines that trigger procurement), that will speed alignment.

Next steps: Ben will propose redline language by EOD tomorrow; Monica will outline options operationally (how opt-outs will be implemented in Hosted vs Dedicated).

Thanks — Laura

Laura / Monica — I reviewed Arbor's annotations briefly and drafted targeted language we can put into the order form (keeps MSA stable, adds a short Exhibit). Key points and proposed approach:

- Ownership: Add explicit "Customer Data & Outputs" definition in Exhibit X. Language: "Customer Data and Customer Outputs shall remain the sole and exclusive property of Customer; no assignment of title is made to Redwood."

- Training: Two-tier approach for order form:
  a) Hosted (standard): "Redwood shall not use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train, refine, or otherwise improve any of Redwood's models unless Customer provides express, written opt-in in the applicable Order Form or Exhibit X."
  b) Dedicated/Private: "Redwood will not train or adapt models on Customer Data or Customer Outputs unless a separate written SOW is executed by both parties."

- Telemetry/Feedback license: Propose narrow telemetry permission for aggregated, de-identified metrics. Add: "Customer may opt out of non-security telemetry by notifying Redwood in writing. Notwithstanding opt-out, Redwood may collect data required to investigate and remediate security incidents or data breaches."

- Audit/evidence: Offer a short compliance exhibit describing how evidence is provided for training/telemetry requests and a quarterly attestation if they choose opt-in.

I've attached a redline with these inserts (marked in green). I'm keeping the language conservative and explicit per Arbor counsel's ask, but we should review commercial impact (e.g., opt-in reduces our ability to improve models with their usage).

Next for operations: Monica — can you confirm whether the opt-out flag is feasible for Hosted customers (UI toggle + API) and how it would affect our logging and audits? Also confirm whether we can reasonably produce quarterly attestation.

Ben

Thanks — quick operational notes to include in the response to Arbor (keeping it short so procurement/legal have what they need):

- Hosted opt-in/opt-out: We can implement an opt-in checkbox at procurement time and an account-level toggle in the Console. Opt-out will stop sending customer prompts/outputs to any analytics pipeline used for model training. Implementation ETA: 3 business days to expose flag in the Console + API; 10 business days for end-to-end QA and docs.

- Dedicated/Private: No model training will occur unless the Account purchases the "Model Adaptation" add-on SOW. We'll call that out explicitly in Exhibit X.

- Telemetry attestation: We can produce a quarterly PDF attestation stating whether any customer data was included in training or model updates, and evidence of aggregation/de-identification procedures. To automate, we'll need a one-off runbook; ETA: 15 business days post-signature.

- Short-term proposal for Arbor: redline language + a 30-day trial of standard Hosted with opt-out enabled by default and an optional opt-in for improvement feedback. That gives them comfort and still keeps the door open commercial.

I'll attach a short snippet file with the Console toggle description. Laura — if Arbor's counsel needs faster turnaround on the doc, I'm happy to hop on a 30-min call with their legal ops.

Monica
